title: Could the proposed COE changes mean higher premiums for all car buyers?
text:
Could the proposed COE changes mean higher premiums for all car buyers? - The Business Times Search
 Subscribe Derryn Wong 
 Subscribe: Could the proposed COE changes mean higher premiums for all car buyers?
 Singapore’s proposed COE changes could push premiums even higher. Automotive consultant Say Kwee Neng explains why.
 Listen . 23:04 Claressa Monteiro 
 Published Tue, Nov 17, 2026 · 05:00 AM Buy a cheaper car and get up to S$15,000 back. Buy a pricier one and pay up to S$15,000 more. That is the idea behind the proposal the Land Transport Authority (LTA) put out in the first week of October, which would merge Category A and Category B of the Certificate of Entitlement (COE) system into one. For mainstream buyers, it sounds like good news. The harder question is what happens at the bidding table.
 The proposals are not final. In this episode of TransportBT , a podcast from The Business Times , Derryn Wong speaks with Say Kwee Neng, an automotive consultant and former car industry executive who has bid in the COE market himself. They look at what the changes are meant to fix, and what they may leave untouched.
 Why listen 
 How we got two categories 
Say traces the history back to 1999, and how the industry kept finding ways around the rules.
 A different diagnosis  
Many people point to Category A and B prices moving closer together. Say has another explanation for the noise, and it changes how the proposal looks.
 Who really sets the price  
Say has seen the closing minutes of a bidding exercise from the inside. He explains who calls the shots, and why merging categories could matter to them.
 Owning versus using  
Say has a view on how the cost of owning a car and the cost of using one should balance, and a clear idea of the outcome he would dread.
 How high could it go  
Wong asks whether S$200,000 is in sight. Say’s answer goes well beyond what happens at the LTA.
 If you are weighing a car purchase, or just wondering why COE prices keep climbing, Say is worth hearing before you place a bid. Listen now.
